title: THEORETICAL INVESTIGATION OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PLACE ATTACHMENT AND WELL-BEING
research_focus: To theoretically investigate the intricate relationship between place attachment and well-being, exploring similarities and differences in theoretical frameworks and practical experiences, and to provide insights for urban planning practices.

sample_context.description: Six participants (three female, three male) aged 20-29, who had been living in the 100. Yıl Neighborhood in Ankara, Turkey for at least 3 years. Participants were selected using purposive sampling based on their ability to provide valuable information relevant to the research questions.
sample_context.setting: A café located on the busiest street in the 100. Yıl Neighborhood, Ankara, Turkey, in close proximity to Middle East Technical University (METU).

findings.description: Social activities, including cultural and artistic opportunities, are important for individuals' attachment to a place, contributing to their sense of self and productivity.
supporting_quotes: Being in contact with too many young people and my need to be productive lead me to engage in social activities. Social activity opportunities are quite important for me. The place where I live provides me with various cultural and social activities.
Music is part of my identity. As a musician, I also see social activities as opportunities to improve myself artistically.

findings.description: Strong social relationships, including family roots and loved ones, contribute to a sense of safety and belonging, which in turn fosters attachment to a place and a feeling of loyalty.
supporting_quotes: I feel safe here because I have family roots, loved ones, and strong social relationships in here. This can be considered a justification for attachment to a place.
I have so many memories in here with the people I love. I feel attached here because I feel like I have a duty of loyalty here.

findings.description: Memories, especially those associated with loved ones and emotional experiences, are crucial for building knowledge about a place and fostering attachment.
supporting_quotes: I think that having knowledge about a place is built on memories. The activities we enjoyed in with our loved ones and some emotional experiences are the things that connect us to the place we live in.

findings.description: Familiarity with a place, including its problems and overall characteristics, contributes to a sense of connectedness and attachment.
supporting_quotes: There are so many things that describe me where I am attached, that I can see myself. I know the problems of this city and neighborhood; I know this place. That is why I am familiar with here in every sense. Being familiar with the place is one of the reasons that explains my connectedness to it.

findings.description: Engaging in active and productive behaviors, especially in nature, enhances feelings of happiness, financial security, awareness, and recognition, contributing to overall well-being.
supporting_quotes: Firstly, being active and productive makes me feel better and happier if I earn something in return. It might be the first example that comes into mind but if I can be active and productive, I can earn money and it is important to feel secured financially.

I enjoy hiking. Being in nature creates an environment that allows me to feel active and think clearly, making me more productive. Even after leaving nature, I return with a sense of awareness, and recognition. I can see the effects of this in my life. It serves as a means for me to make an impact for myself or others and all these processes enables me to feel good about myself.

findings.description: Feeling connected with others, whether familiar or strangers, in a shared space and time, increases productivity, fosters common solutions, and enhances feelings of happiness and safety.
supporting_quotes: Firstly, the sense of togetherness is undoubtedly significant both individually and socially. However, for me, it can be considered as the key to many things. The feeling of being together with either people I know well or strangers, sharing a common space and time, increases my productivity. Searching for common solutions with these people and helping others makes me feel good. At the same time, knowing that we are together and I am not alone makes me basically feel happy and safe.

findings.antecedent: Pleasure and aesthetics of a place
findings.description: Enjoying life, including the aesthetics of a place and general feelings of enjoyment, directly contributes to happiness and overall well-being.
supporting_quotes: I think enjoying life in every aspect is directly related to happiness and feeling good. It may be difficult to express this but I will try to describe this pleasantness. What I mean by pleasure can sometimes be result of viewing the aesthetics of a place, and sometimes it can be described as a feeling of enjoyment that arises as a result of any situation. This feeling of pleasure triggers my happiness and I feel better in some way.

findings.theme_name: Territoriality and feeling like a homeowner
findings.description: Feeling a sense of ownership and belonging to a place, akin to being a homeowner, contributes to feeling better and happier, as opposed to feeling like a guest or stranger.
supporting_quotes: When I think of this place where I am attached to, I feel like at home. I have a sense of ownership here. I experience the same thing when I establish a sense of togetherness with the people I am with here. It is impossible for me to feel this way when I am in a place where I feel like a guest or a stranger. Feeling like a homeowner makes me feel better and happier.

findings.antecedent: Being understood and accepted by others
findings.description: The feeling of being understood, accepted, and recognized by loved ones and within a social structure provides a crucial sense of security, which is fundamental for psychological and mental well-being.
supporting_quotes: My conclusion from this work is as follows: I realized how important it is for me to be understood. Of course, it is important for every individual, but it is critical for me. When I look at the relationships I have established in general, I have associated this concept with many other concepts. I cannot feel myself belonging to that social structure where I am not understood, and I also need this sense of belonging. Although I feel sufficient and successful in some things, I also feel deficiencies in some things. To feel good about myself, I also need people who can fill this gap.

For me, feeling safe was the prominent concept, I think. When I think about both being understood, being accepted, and my loved ones, these concepts that provide me with this sense of security are the factors that make me feel good. The fact that my loved ones and family are here and that I feel understood and accepted also shows that this place provides me with these things. Because when I don't feel safe, I am really negatively affected psychologically and mentally. When I look at it in general, attachment to a place and well-being overlap a lot, I think. Because, for example, to feel attached to a place, I need to feel safe and free. When I feel this way, I feel good...

findings.description: Feeling freedom and achieving economic welfare are crucial for an individual's well-being, as financial situations often underpin the ability to fulfill various needs.
supporting_quotes: I think freedom is very important for me. A person needs to feel freedom to feel good about themselves. Of course, this freedom is related to many things, but reaching a level of economic welfare is also very important. Because fulfilling many needs is somewhat dependent on financial situations.

findings.description: Experiencing nature allows individuals to enter a state of 'flow,' promoting clarity of thought, productivity, and overall well-being, which city life often hinders.
supporting_quotes: I realized that I feel better in nature. Because when I am in nature, I can stay in the flow, but city life does not allow this much. I am connected to both the city and the nature where I spend time, but both of them meet my different needs according to the context of the place. In nature, it is to stay in the flow, while in the city, social relationships and the sense of togetherness I establish are more satisfying. Therefore, different things make me feel good in both.

mechanism_candidates: The accumulation of experience and meaning affects individual’s perception, values, ideas, attitudes, and behavior patterns, establishing a person-place relationship.
Place attachment contributes to one’s sense of the self when the strength of the bond and the meaning of place to individual has increased.
Affective, cognitive, and behavioral psychological processes mediate the bond between people and place.
Social relationships and group identity are facilitated by place attachment, leading to a sense of community.
Self-actualization and esteem needs, as per Maslow's Hierarchy, are fulfilled through place experiences, contributing to well-being.
Perceptive cognitional mechanisms (perceptions, thoughts, memories, schemas) shape understanding of the environment and influence place attachment and well-being.
Emotions (positive and negative) influence place experience and evaluations, impacting attachment and well-being.
Behaviors (e.g., involvement in decision-making, pro-environmental actions, proximity-maintaining, reconstruction) are influenced by place attachment and contribute to well-being.
Cultural context, shared meanings, and symbolic connections foster collective identity and belongingness, strengthening place attachment and social well-being.
The sense of belonging and security engendered by social connections and place attachment improves overall well-being and reduces negative psychological states.
transferability_limits: Findings may be influenced by mood fluctuations and occasion-specific influences, limiting generalizability.
The study's homogeneous age group (20-29 young adults) and collectivist cultural context (Turkey) may lead to different concept emphases compared to other demographics or individualistic cultures.
Concepts like 'belonging' or 'roots' might be more prominent for middle-aged and older people in the Turkish context, which were superficially mentioned by the young adult participants.
The dominance of Western sources in the literature review might limit the representation of diverse cultural perspectives on place attachment and well-being.
limitations: The study's methodology, particularly the fuzzy cognitive mapping technique, may be influenced by individuals' mood fluctuations and occasion-specific influences, potentially affecting the generalizability of findings.
The atmosphere of the study place or current social events could influence participants' responses.

The selection of a specific, homogeneous age group (20-29 young adults) may have led to an emphasis on certain concepts (e.g., social activities, having fun) while others (e.g., belonging, roots for older generations) were less prominent.
The theoretical framework primarily relies on Western research, which may not fully capture the nuances of place attachment and well-being in collectivist cultures like Turkey.

The exemplified focus group study, while providing rich qualitative data, is limited in its ability to provide diverse results that might be obtained from a more heterogeneous social and cultural group.
